 Judgment

The appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal against the judgment and award dated 12.01.2021 passed in MVC No.37/2019 by the Court of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.3 and Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Ballari (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to as per their status and rank before the Appellate Court.
3. The brief facts of the case are that:

On 26.08.2018 at about 10.30 p.m., when the deceased was proceeding in his TVS Super XL Moped motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-34-W-3504 from Ballari to Adoni and when he reached near Haligera Bus stop, on Adoni-Aspari Road, Aspari Mandal,
at that time, the respondent No.1 being the driver of KSRTC bus bearing R e g . N o . K A - 5 7 - F - 8 6 8 c a m e f r o m o p p o s i t e d i r e c t i o n i n h i g h N C :
2023:KHC-D:9103-DB speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motorcycle, as a result of which the deceased fell down and sustained severe nature of head injuries and also sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately, he was shifted to hospital, but the doctors declared that the injured is dead.
Therefore, the claimants have filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation on account of death of Nagaraja.
4. On hearing both sides, the Tribunal has partly allowed the appeal by awarding compensation of Rs.12,05,056/- with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the appellants have preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has not awarded the compensation in accordance with law and facts.
The age of the deceased NC: 2023:KHC-D:9103-DB was 41 years and was earning Rs.21,000/- p.m. by doing dhobi work.
But the Court below has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- p.m.

The Tribunal has not awarded compensation for future prospects as per the decision held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has also not awarded just and fair compensation as per the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court.
On all these grounds, he sought to allow this appeal and to enhance the compensation.

As against this, the learned counsel for the respondent-insurance company submits that the Tribunal has passed the judgment and award in accordance with law and facts and that there are no grounds to interfere with the same.
On this ground, he sought to dismiss the appeal.
8. We have carefully examined the materials placed before this Court.
The age of the deceased was 41 years as per post- mortem report.

Accordingly, the Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier as per the dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION LIMITED AND ANOTHER reported in (2009)6 SCC 121.
9.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION LIMITED AND ANOTHER reported in (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
With regard to the income of the deceased is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed at Rs.10,000/-
p.m. which is not in consonance with the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

In view of guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income of Rs.11,750/- p.m. has to be taken into consideration and in view of Pranay Sethi's case (supra), 25% has to be added towards future prospects.
1/3 has to be deducted as the number of dependents are three.
Then it comes to Rs.9,792/- (14,698/3).
The appropriate multiplier is 14.

Therefore, NC: 2023:KHC-D:9103-DB the loss of dependency is reassessed and quantified as follows:
9792x12x14 = Rs.16,45,056/-
10.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also keeping in mind the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, it is just and proper to award compensation as under:
 Sl. Heads Amount No. (in Rs.)
1
Loss of dependency 16,45,056.00 2 Loss of estate 15,000.00 3
Towards funeral expenses and 15,000.00  transportation of body 4
Towards loss of consortium 1,20,000.00  (40,000x3)
11. Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,95,056/- instead of Rs.12,05,056/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing petition till its realization.

Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:9103-DB ORDER i. Appeal allowed in part.
ii. Judgment and award dated 12.01.2021 passed in MVC No.37/2019 on the file of the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal No.3 and Prl. Senior Civil Judge & CJM, Ballari,
